description: Structural governance plan for active large assets. Indexing is a mitigation, not a complete lifecycle decision.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep index-first access now; when editing an area, prefer extracting cohesive helper/check modules instead of adding more unrelated cases to the monolith.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: Any single new tranche adding more than 300 lines or 5 cases to the monolith must consider a domain shard.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep as the unified closeout runtime until the runtime package split is ready; new sizeable features should be extracted into focused helper modules instead of expanding this script.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: If the file grows above 65KB or receives another lifecycle feature, extract observability, notification, or audit helpers behind the same closeout-cap facade.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep lessons.md as a lightweight first-read index with legacy L-number redirects; store full lesson bodies in compass/knowledge/lessons/<l-id>.md modules.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When the lightweight index exceeds 50KB, split topic catalogs further while preserving legacy L-number anchors.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep CONTRIBUTING.md as the authority source, but move startup-critical rules into CONTRIBUTING.core.md and route all other reads by section.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When a new section duplicates an existing gate or first-read rule, merge or route instead of expanding the startup surface.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep as the human-readable locator for critical RedCap files. Agents should search exact terms or use the machine policy/checker instead of reading the whole dictionary during startup.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When the dictionary exceeds 75KB, split the human view by section while preserving references/file-lookup-dictionary-policy.json as the machine source.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep as the machine-readable coverage source for File Lookup Dictionary. Agents should query it through redcap-file-lookup-dictionary-check or targeted path search, not read the whole policy during startup.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When the policy exceeds 75KB or required_paths exceeds 220 entries, split required path rows by section behind the same checker interface.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep as the generated first-read index for docs archaeology; agents must consume summary/plan/budget commands instead of pasting or bulk-loading the full JSON into context.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When catalog.json exceeds 100KB, evaluate compact index shards or a generated SQLite/FTS sidecar while preserving the same summary/plan/budget interface.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep Layer A dispatcher details scoped and prevent RedCap self-development from relying on full-file startup import.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When RedCap self-development rules are added, prefer CONTRIBUTING.core.md or a targeted reference over expanding top-level SKILL.md.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep as the machine-readable guarantee registry while routing human explanation through File Lookup Dictionary; if the registry keeps growing, split inactive/deprecated guarantees into an archive registry consumed by the same validator.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When the registry exceeds 75KB or when more than 5 new guarantees are added in one tranche, evaluate category sharding with a generated combined view.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep as the P4-29 copy-first internal contract mirror for execution guarantees. Do not auto-import or bulk-read it; use the old references anchor or the P4-29 copy-first checker for exact verification until a future delete-last task changes authority.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When the old references/execution-guarantees.json anchor is retired or this mirror becomes the primary runtime contract, split or index it before making it a startup-readable artifact.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep as the active architecture-smell governance registry while exposing human progress through current-status and task reports. Do not bulk-read the full backlog during startup; use exact RASG ids or status summaries.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When the backlog exceeds 75KB, split closed items into an archive registry and keep only open/current decision records in the active file behind the same current-status surface.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep as the machine-readable long-horizon framework upgrade route map while exposing human progress through the generated framework-upgrade spec block and current-status. Agents must query exact P ids or the progress meter instead of bulk-reading the full backlog during startup.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When the backlog exceeds 75KB or when another 10 closed P4 items accumulate, split closed historical route entries into an archived registry consumed by the same backlog checker and keep active/current route items in the live authority.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep as the umbrella validator facade, but do not add substantial new validation logic inline. New release-readiness checks should live in focused redcap-*-check modules and spec-check should only route to them.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When spec-check grows above 60KB or gains more than 10 new route-only invocations, split release-readiness route checks into a sourced shard or generated check registry while preserving the same public command.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep as a generated file-level preflight ledger, not a startup document. Agents must discover it through File Lookup Dictionary or run redcap-legacy-asset-migration-apply-plan.sh; do not bulk-read it unless auditing a specific migration item.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When this manifest becomes human-read frequently, exceeds 350KB, or item count exceeds 300, split it into generated shards with a compact summary index while preserving the same checker interface.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep as a compact rehearsal receipt for alias-map and rollback proof, not a startup document. Agents should read the summary first and only inspect specific alias rows when auditing a migration item.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When the alias_map exceeds 150 entries or the file exceeds 150KB, shard alias rows into generated detail files with a compact summary index and preserve the same rehearsal checker interface.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep as a compact git-worktree rehearsal receipt, not a startup document. Agents should inspect summary/catalog_anchor_validation first and only open specific alias rows when auditing a migration item.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When the alias_map exceeds 150 entries or the file exceeds 150KB, shard alias rows into generated detail files with a compact summary index and preserve the same worktree rehearsal checker interface.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep as a generated resolver manifest, not a startup document. Agents should read the docs catalog legacy_alias_resolver summary first, then use redcap-legacy-asset-alias-resolver.sh --resolve for specific old/new paths.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When alias entries exceed 150 or the file exceeds 150KB, shard entry details behind the same resolver command while preserving a compact manifest summary.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep as a compact copy-first apply receipt, not a startup document. Agents should inspect summary first and use redcap-legacy-asset-main-tree-apply.sh --check-result for full verification.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When copy entries exceed 150 or the file exceeds 150KB, shard entry details behind the same apply checker while preserving a compact receipt summary.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep as the generated delete-last safety receipt, not a startup document. Agents should inspect summary first and use redcap-legacy-asset-delete-last-preflight.sh --check-result for full verification.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When reference_scan exceeds 150 rows or the file exceeds 150KB, shard scan details behind the same preflight checker while preserving a compact summary receipt.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep as the generated delete-last apply receipt, not a startup document. Agents should inspect summary first and use redcap-legacy-asset-delete-last-apply.sh --check-result for full verification.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When delete entries exceed 150 or the file exceeds 150KB, shard entry details behind the same apply checker while preserving a compact receipt summary.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep the R1 control-plane dry-run manifest as a machine-readable generated map, not a startup document. Agents should inspect summary fields or run redcap-r1-control-plane-contract-split-check.sh; only open specific entries when auditing a future control-plane move tranche.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When dry-run entries exceed 250 or the file exceeds 150KB, shard entries into generated detail files behind the same checker while preserving a compact preflight summary.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep as the lightweight formal Prism report index for status and degradation checks. Agents should read it through prism archive/degradation checkers or exact report id searches instead of bulk-loading it during startup.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When the index exceeds 75KB or formal report rows exceed 50, split archived legacy rows into a generated archive shard while preserving prism/reports/index.yaml as the compact current-window index.

assets.structural_strategy: Keep as a private copy-first target, not a startup document. Agents should discover it through the alias resolver or File Lookup Dictionary and only open it when auditing that exact historical closeout lineage.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: If private-archive/redcap-knowledge gains multiple large private copies, add a generated private archive index or shard policy instead of relying on per-file exceptions.

assets.structural_strategy: Preserve formal evidence and any named local evidence referenced by tracked reports or knowledge assets. Prune acceptance fixtures after tests, and review only unreferenced named evidence after the retention threshold with inventory/prune-local dry-run first.
assets.trigger_for_revisit: When ignored prism/runs exceeds warn thresholds, run lifecycle summary and prune only tool-classified safe targets; physical prune-local --apply requires explicit user approval and must not break evidence references.
